 Judgment

The instant Criminal Revision is directed against the judgment and order dated 10.03.2015 passed by Shri Pankaj Kumar-II, the learned District & Additional Sessions Judge-III, Godda passed in Criminal Appeal Nos. 52 of 2014 and 26 of 2014, whereby and whereunder, learned Additional Sessions Judge-III, Godda has modified the sentence imposed upon the petitioner for the offence under section 498A of IPC from R.I. of 2 years to R.I. 1 year along with fine and default stipulation.

sentences.text: 2. The prosecution story as depicted in the FIR arising out of complaint lodged by the complainant Bibi Jubeda Khatoon is that the prosecutrix was married with the present petitioner in accordance with Muslim rites and customs and she blessed with one son.

It is further alleged that just after few days of marriage, the present petitioner and in-laws of the prosecutrix started subjecting her to cruelty both physically and mentally due to non-fulfillment 2 Criminal Revision No.671 of 2015 of additional dowry of Rs.40,000/- cash and one Hero Honda Motrocycle and ousted her from matrimonial home.

It is further alleged that the villagers attempted to pacify and settle the dispute in pursuance of which present petitioner came to his Sasural on 16.01.2005 and stayed in the night after taking dinner.
At about 11:00 hours, the prosecutrix and the present petitioner went to sleep in a separate room then the petitioner aged her mouth by putting cloths and started assaulting brutally.
In the meanwhile, other family members woke up then present petitioner opened the door and went out of the room with threatening of dire consequences to the prosecutrix and her family members.
The prosecutrix got primary aid at Mahgema and thereafter she went to police station but was advised to lodge the case in the court.

Hence, the complaint case was lodged, which was sent by the concerned court under section 156(3) of Cr.PC for registration and investigation of the case and the same was registered as Mohagama P.S. Case No.23 of 2005.

3. After completion of investigation, charge-sheet was submitted against the petitioner along with six others who happens to be close relatives of the petitioner for the offences under sections 498A and 406 of IPC and Sections 3/4 of D.P. Act.
After hearing, the charge under section 498A read with section 34 of IPC alone was framed against all accused persons.

4. In course of trial, all together 7 witnesses have been examined by the prosecution apart from the documentary evidence, Ext. A endorsement of complaint petition for registration of case and Ext. 2,
formal FIR.
3
Criminal Revision No.671 of 2015
No oral or documentary evidence has been adduced by the defence.
The case of defence is denial from occurrence and false implication and plea of innocence.

5. Learned trial court after conclusion of trial acquitted all other accused persons but the petitioner was held guilty for the offence under section 498A of IPC and sentenced with imprisonment as stated above.
The appeal of the petitioner was also dismissed by the Additional Sessions Judge on merits but reduce the sentence.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner has very stoutly argued that it is a burning case of misuse of provision of 498A of IPC.

The prosecutrix, who has been examined as (P.W-1) has categorically admitted that she remained peacefully at her matrimonial home till 2 years but in the complaint petition, she states that just after marriage, she was subjected to cruelty and torture.
In what manner, she was subjected to cruelty at her matrimonial home has not been specified rather she also admits that she has one child, who is living with the present petitioner very properly.

The prosecutrix has concocted very cleverly a false story that the petitioner went to her parental home where he attempted to assault her by gagging her mouth and she was subjected to cruelty at the hands of him.

Admittedly, the marriage of prosecutrix was solemnized in the year 1993 and the story of demand and torture is alleged to have happened in the year 2005 due to some domestic disputes and ordinary wear and tear in life.
7. It is further submitted that the own cousin of the prosecutrix examined as P.W.3 has categorically stated that the prosecutrix has stayed at her matrimonial home only for one year.
Thereafter, she came to the house of 4 Criminal Revision No.671 of 2015 his uncle.
The close relatives of the prosecutrix have given contradictory statements regarding demand of motorcycle and torture meted with the prosecutrix at the hands of petitioner.

The petitioner was also under judicial custody during the trial of the case from 28.03.2007 to 17.05.2007 and after conviction from 24.09.2015 to 03.11.2015 when he was released on bail vide order dated 03.11.2015 passed in this revision application.

It is further submitted that both courts below have failed to appreciate the ingredients of section 498A of IPC has not been proved in this case against the petitioner beyond all reasonable doubts, which suffers from perversity.
8. The prosecutrix was served with notice in this case but she declined to take the notice and participate in the proceedings, which also indicates her non- co-operation in the legal proceedings.
The petitioner has suffered very much in the whole proceedings of this case and has been sufficiently punished.
Hence, this revision may be allowed setting aside the impugned judgment and orders.

sentences.text: On the other hands, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the aforesaid contentions raised on behalf of the petitioner.

10.For the better appreciation of the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, the relevant provision of section 498A of IPC is extracted as under:-
498-A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.-
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
5 Criminal Revision No.671 of 2015 Explanation.-

For the purpose of this section,
"cruelty" means- (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause gave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.]

11. In the instant case, although charge has been framed against the petitioner for the offences under sections 498A r/w section 34 of Indian Penal Code, which appears appropriate to be quoted hereunder:
(i) Firstly, that you on or about from 1995 to 16.01.2005 at village Ramkole P.S.
Mahagama District-Godda, you being husband of Bibi Jubaida Khatoon and the relatives of the husband subjected her to cruelty with the said Bibi Jubaida Khatoon in prosecution of common intention you all.
(ii) And thereby committed offence punishable under section 498A r/w 34 of IPC and within my cognizance.

13.In view of the above background, it appears necessary in the ends of justice to discuss some relevant evidence of witnesses examined by the prosecution for the purpose of arriving at just decision.

14.P.W.1 is the prosecutrix, she admits that her marriage was solemnized with the petitioner in the year 1993 and she also admits that in her matrimonial home, she remained quite well for about 2 years, thereafter, her husband demanded Rs.40,000/- cash or a Rajdoot motorcycle.
She further alleged that in the year 2005, she was ousted from her matrimonial home then she lodged this case from her parental home.
In her cross-examination, she has categorically admitted that she remained quite well in her matrimonial home only for about 2 years, thereafter she returned to her parental house.
She also admits that her husband owned a tractor for agricultural purpose and she has one son, who is residing with the petitioner quite well.

She can not tell the specific day, date or year when she was asked for Rs.40,000/- as additional dowry and she has denied the suggestion of defence that due to some matrimonial dispute and differences in matrimonial relationship with her husband, she has lodged this false case as no such occurrence ever took place.

15.It is very disastrous to observe here that in the entire evidence, the prosecutrix has not stated about the main incident 17.01.2005, when her husband came to her parental home and in the night,
petitioner gagged her 7 Criminal Revision No.671 of 2015 mouth and attempted to kill her which has been made cause of action in this case.
It is admitted facts that she was residing at her parental home just after 2 years of marriage since 1995.
16.The
brother of the prosecutrix-Md. Samim (PW 2) has stated that due to domestic scuffles in the matrimonial relationship, his sister was ousted from matrimonial home.

This witness was cross-examined on 04.03.2013 and on that date, he admits that the son of prosecutrix and petitioner was about 16 years old, and in his cross examination, he admits that due to domestic disputes, his sister was residing at her parental home.
17. P.W.6 Md. Rizwan is an independent witness, according to his evidence, he admits that about 2 years, the prosecutrix lived at her matrimonial home quite well.
Thereafter, some money was asked by her husband but he has not specifically stated any amount.
18.P.W.7 Md. Manjur Alam, who happens to be cousin brother of the prosecutrix has stated about the demand of Rs.20,000/- as additional dowry.

19.From the aforesaid discussion, it is crystal clear that the prosecutrix has given a colourable statement regarding demand of cash or motorcycle by the petitioner and consequent torture meted to her, she has also no specific version that the petitioner came to her parental home where, he also reiterated the demand of dowry and assaulted her in cruel manner by gagging her mount.

20.Learned trial court in the statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.PC of the present petitioner has posed a general and omnibus question, which does not contain any willful conduct of the Md. 4 petitioner or any specific act of subjecting the prosecutrix to harassment for physical or mental torture due to 8 Criminal Revision No.671 of 2015 non-fulfillment of any illegal demand.

sentences.text:
Similarly,
the appellate court has also reiterated in-toto, the findings of learned trial court without taking pain to act as a court of facts being First Appellate Court and failed to discharge onerous burden upon the first Appellate Court.
It is crystal clear that the present petitioner has been held guilty and sentenced for no offence at all.
The ingredients of offence under section 498A of IPC or not constituted in the facts and circumstances as proved by prosecution.
Therefore, I am constrained to set aside the order of the courts below sentencing the present appellant for the offence under section 498A of IPC.

Accordingly, this revision is allowed the impugn judgment and order passed by the trail court, which is hereby set aside and petitioner is set at liberty acquitting from the charges leveled against him and also discharge from liability of bail bond.

21.Let the copy of this order along with record of trial court be sent back for information and needful.
(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Jharkhand High Court, at Ranchi Date: 15 / 05 /2024 Pappu/-
